description: One-pole IIR low pass on signed 11-bit samples: x=a[10:0], gain g=b[10:0] as an unsigned Q10 coefficient (unity at 1024, up to 1.999); all other bits of a and b are don't care. state[10:0] holds the previous output y and c[31] seeds it from x instead (filter restart). e=x-y, delta=round_half_up(e*g>>>10), y_new=clamp_s11(y+delta). result[10:0]=y_new, result[31:11]=0. aux[11:0]=e, aux[12]=clamped high, aux[13]=clamped low, aux[26:14]=delta, aux[31:26]=0. fault=1 only when the 11-bit output saturated, which needs a gain above about 1.5.
hardware_advantage: A recursive filter needs its feedback loop closed inside one enabled beat; the slice does multiply-then-accumulate every cycle, which a soft-processor loop cannot sustain at a fixed control rate.
provenance: original source authored in this workspace; no third-party RTL imported
qualification: engineering candidate; not certified production or side-channel protection
